title: Bada al-Islam ghariban fa-tuba li-l-ghuraba'
behavior_type: الشعور بالاختلاف عن الأصدقاء بسبب الالتزام
reference_info: صحيح مسلم، حديث رقم 145، عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه
text_original: بدأ الإسلام غريبًا وسيعود غريبًا كما بدأ، فطوبى للغرباء. رواه مسلم (145) عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه.
text_simplified: When your child feels like a stranger because he is the only one in his company who prays or observes hijab, teach him the hadith of the Prophet ﷺ: «Bada al-Islam ghariban wa-sa-ya‘udu ghariban kama bada’a, fa-tuba li-l-ghuraba’» (reported by Muslim). Explain to him that differing from the majority in obedience to Allah is not a deficiency, but rather the praise with which the Prophet ﷺ promised the committed in every era.

review_defects.why: The title is transliterated but not translated; the English reader cannot understand the meaning of the hadith phrase.

review_defects.arabic: «بدأ الإسلام غريبًا وسيعود غريبًا كما بدأ، فطوبى للغرباء»
review_defects.english: «Bada al-Islam ghariban wa-sa-ya‘udu ghariban kama bada’a, fa-tuba li-l-ghuraba’»
review_defects.why: The hadith is transliterated but not translated; the English reader cannot understand its meaning, so the instruction to teach the hadith is not fulfilled.

review_defects.english: the Prophet ﷺ promised the committed
review_defects.why: بشّر means 'gave glad tidings' or 'announced good news', not 'promised'; 'promised' changes the meaning.

review_defects.arabic: اشرح له أن الاختلاف عن الأغلبية في طاعة الله ليس نقصًا بل هو المديح الذي بشّر به النبي ﷺ الملتزمين في كل زمان.
review_defects.english: Explain to him that differing from the majority in obedience to Allah is not a deficiency, but rather the praise with which the Prophet ﷺ promised the committed in every era.
review_defects.why: The phrase 'the committed' is stiff and unnatural; the Arabic is warm and direct, using 'الملتزمين' as a natural noun.
